name_ru: Ту Линь Фэн Хуан То Ча
processing: Pressed into the bowl-shaped tuo by the Tulin factory in Nanjian. Raw and ripe versions are both made, with ripe ones sold under recipe numbers such as 8502.
harvest_season: Varies by batch and recipe; factory tuos are usually not sold by picking season.
appearance_dry: A compact bowl-shaped tuo of dark olive to brown leaf, darker in ripe versions.
appearance_liquor: Golden to amber in raw tuos, and deep red-brown in ripe ones.
appearance_wet: Chopped and whole leaf pieces, as is usual in factory tuos.
taste_profile: Published tasting notes are thin. Typical of factory raw tuocha, young raw versions are strong and somewhat smoky-bitter, and they soften with age, while ripe tuos are earthy and smooth.

brewing.notes: Tuos are pressed hard, so break them up with a pick and let the pieces rest. Keep young raw versions to very short first steeps.

vintage_note: Sold by production year and, often, recipe number or batch code. Older raw and ripe lots from the 2000s, such as 2002 and 2004 tuos, are still on the market alongside current production. Check whether a given tuo is raw or ripe, because the same brand name covers both.
description:
This is the signature tuocha of the Tulin brand from Nanjian, in the south of Dali prefecture. Phoenix refers to the product line, and the tea is a factory tuo, compact and reliable rather than a single-origin showpiece.

Little is published about the raw material or the exact recipes. It follows the familiar pattern of Yunnan factory tuocha: leaf blended to a house style and pressed hard into a bowl shape. Tulin makes the tuo both raw and ripe, and it sells numbered recipes such as 8502.

In the cup, expect what factory tuos typically give. Raw is firm, bitter and a little sharp when young, and calmer with storage; ripe is earthy and smooth. Hard pressing means you should open the tuo before steeping, or the first cups will be weak and the later ones overdone.

This is a good everyday or storage tea when you know what you are getting. Look for the year and recipe number on the wrapper, and be sceptical of old tuos with no history of how they were kept.
history:
Company accounts say the state-run Nanjian County Tea Factory was founded in 1985 and began making the Tulin Phoenix tuo that year. The Tulin trademark is dated to 1986 in some accounts and 1987 in others.

The factory's team and brand passed into a county tea company in 1991, a shareholding cooperative in 1997, and Yunnan Tulin Tea Co., Ltd in 2007. Most of this history comes from the company and its sellers rather than from independent research.
